explanation: A squid's two extra limbs are long feeding tentacles that shoot out to snatch prey, gripping with suckers and, in some species, hooks. Octopuses have only their eight arms.

claims.text: A squid has ten limbs: eight arms and two longer feeding tentacles.
An octopus has eight arms and no tentacles.
Squid feeding tentacles shoot out to catch prey and grip it with suckers, which in some species carry hooks.

issues.note: 'Limbs' stands for arms plus tentacles, as the measure line says, but the stem alone does not. A player who counts only arms sees a tie at eight each. Naming 'arms and tentacles' (or 'appendages') in the stem would remove the trick reading.
